categories_thin: Manufacturing, labs and wholesale: still the thinnest group. Only Parkway-Kew (own site + NJMEP profile), Atlantic Precision Technology (directories) and AC Compacting Equipment (own site) could be named. The Jersey Ave / Excelsior Ave / Quarry Ln industrial parks have almost no public directory presence, so expect misses among small job shops.

Event venues: two independent venues listed (Eagle's Landing Events & Picnics, N Brunswick Social Club by Daliza). Larger banquet halls in town are mostly attached to hotels and were excluded as chain-flagged; a smaller venue seen only in a wedding-vendor listing (Zola) could not be tied to a North Brunswick street address.

Repair services: only three (vacuum/sewing, phone repair, shoe repair), and the shoe repair's current operation is uncertain. No appliance-repair shop inside town surfaced - the nearest independent counters are listed at 600 Jersey Ave, which is New Brunswick, not North Brunswick.
Independent retail: town retail is dominated by big-box centres; most small-shop entries remain directory-only, so both misses and closed shops are likely.
Music and art schools: added Ilana Visotsky Art Studio this pass, but most remaining entries are single-instructor studios with no street address published.
caveats: Entries removed from the previous version, with reasons: Circle Motel (no North Brunswick address, phone or independent page could be found); Adorable Doos (its own site places the salon at 332 Ridge Rd, Dayton, so it belongs to the Dayton/South Brunswick zone); Minuteman Press North Brunswick (franchise location, excluded); The Ashi (now an Ascend Collection hotel, a Choice Hotels brand, excluded as chain-flagged); All American Pet Resorts North Brunswick (franchised brand with franchise-development material on its own site, local ownership unverifiable); Nam-It Engraving (the company's own contact page gives South River, NJ 08882, by appointment only, so the 1520 Jersey Ave record is stale and it is out of zone); Brunswick Sign & Exhibit Corp. (own site gives 20 George Street, South River NJ 08882, with 1510 Jersey Ave only in older listings).

Costello's Ace Hardware is kept but explicitly labelled: Ace is a retailer-owned co-op and this operator runs several New Jersey stores under the Costello's Ace name, so it is a multi-store Ace dealer rather than a one-site independent. Drop it if the chain test is applied strictly.

Explicit in/out decision on laundry: dry cleaners and tailoring/alteration shops are treated as in scope for group D and are listed (five cleaners plus two tailors). Laundry is not on the exclusion list and these are ordinary local service businesses; remove them if the owner wants only shops selling goods.

Martial arts schools are given group D here to sit with the dance, music and driving schools, although the category list files martial arts studios under group B. They were added because the verifier flagged the coverage gap.
Balaji Flowers links DoorDash from its own site; it is kept as a florist/gift retailer rather than a delivery-app food business, but it is a borderline case under that exclusion.

NJ Leaf and Costello's Ace Hardware both publish 1345 US-1 as their street address. Both come from the businesses' own sites, so the address was not altered, but a triage call should confirm the unit/suite.

Another batch of entries still rests on one or two bulk directories only (DClase Joyeria, East Avenue, Rachel Boutique, AC Vintage Clothing, NAYAB Couture, Always New For You, Anything ZYX1, Alternative Gifts, Aap Carpet, Carpet Plus, Carpet & Futon Gallery, Grooming Tails, View A Miracle, Galis Photography, NJ Ballet Arts, Accelr8, Teach Me Driving, Little Spring Montessori, Rainbow Academy, North Brunswick Florist & Gift, Dee's Flowers, Duchess Florals, Golden Tiger Karate, Family Karate Center, Go For It Kickboxing, A & M Discount Vacuum, Smart Phone Doctor, Atlantic Precision). Their active_evidence field says so; the triage team should confirm each before outreach.

Duchess Florals and Cha Cha Gifts each carry a directory signal that they may be temporarily or permanently closed, and North Brunswick Cobbler Shop has no review later than 2023 plus a local post saying the Livingston Ave cobbler left. All three are kept with the doubt recorded rather than silently dropped.
Hotels: only Farrington Inn is a plausible independent; the Route 1 properties are chain-flagged. Farrington's independent ownership could not be verified from any page.
Phones are recorded only where a listing or the business's own page displayed them; a number of small shops publish no phone, so 'Unknown' appears several times.
data_gaps: Yellow Pages, Superpages, Cylex, Manta, BBB and localitybiz returned HTTP 403 to direct fetches throughout, so their content is reflected only through search-result snippets. Phone numbers attributed to those profiles were not visually confirmed on the profile pages themselves.
Google Maps and Bing Maps result lists were not harvested this pass; only web search plus open directory pages were used, so some small shops with no directory presence are likely missing.
Overpass/OpenStreetMap was not re-queried this pass after repeated rate-limiting in the earlier round; the old OSM-derived record for NJ Leaf was replaced with the dispensary's own page.

North Brunswick Township's own website (licensed-business or economic-development lists) was not reached, and the Shoppes at North Brunswick tenant directory still returns almost no usable text, so that centre's independent tenants are probably under-represented.
NJ Business Directory pagination returns identical first-page content, so roughly 60 of its 87 North Brunswick listings were never reviewed.
D&B's count of North Brunswick manufacturers could not be opened; only firms corroborated elsewhere were added.
Nam-It Engraving and Brunswick Sign & Exhibit moved out of town according to their own sites; they were dropped here rather than carried, and should be picked up by whichever zone covers South River.
